items.title: William "Ba Ba" Ridgley Interview, 1961-04-07
items.q: Silver Leaf after we organized our home. I think the band kind of went to pieces after that. Because Celestine and I both left, you see.

ctx.x: They might not even have told you. That's possible too. Well, who took your place when you left? Do you remember that?

Silver Leaf. Yeah. I don't know who they did get to play trombone after I left them. Silver Leaf after we organized our home. I think the band kind of went to pieces after that. Because Celestine and I both left, you see. I don't think they ever got that band together anymore. But Albert Battista. George Sayles, the manager of his daddy, and a bass violin player by the name of Oscar Alps.
What did George Sayles play? What instruments? Banger, a guitar.

items.title: William "Ba Ba" Ridgley Interview, 1959-06-02
items.q: And our band, Celestine, was leader. William Ridgely was a bookie agent and businessman.

ctx.x: Piano. Piano. And our band, Celestine, was leader. William Ridgely was a bookie agent and businessman. And we went a real good long ways like that until the climax came in 25. That's when the original Tuxedo Band split. Then we had two bands.
Oh yes, I heard about that. Did you take over the original band then?

items.title: William "Ba Ba" Ridgley Interview, 1961-04-11
items.q: Oh, Solistan was in my lifetime playing first. You see, Solistan leaving my band and I didn't care where he would go, I'd always have open for him.

ctx.x: Oh, Solistan was in my lifetime playing first. You see, Solistan leaving my band and I didn't care where he would go, I'd always have open for him. When he come back, well he got ready to come back to the band and they all well understood that. They never did try to keep them out. You know, if he got out of the job he used to come right on back. But we started together and both of us was coming to boys and I kept the band going. He used to come right on back whenever he got ready. He left me about three or four…
Could you give me that picture of Thomas' man?
